name: truenorth
display_name: IBM TrueNorth (28 nm, Merolla 2014), 4096 cores of 256 x 256 on a 64 x 64 mesh

faithfulness.note: TrueNorth weighs a binary synapse by one of four per-neuron axon-type weights. The registered geometry declares 1-bit weights (scout_chip.md section 5.2), so a weight-quantized program on the bundle is not the weight law of TrueNorth. A signed 1-bit grid has no nonzero level (q_max 0), so both doors refuse weight quantization on the bundle by name (the applied schema of weight_bits, key amendment K1), and a float deployment applies no weight grid, while its payload sizes, pricing and record read weight_bits=1 (a 1-bit cell, which pricing a float run states as a boundary owned by G3), which its label names (key amendment K2). The floorplan is the 4096 cores of the profile on a 64 x 64 mesh, one core per tile (truenorth.json validity).

notes: allow_coalescing and allow_neuron_splitting are false: merolla2014a describes the core as "a self-contained neural network with 256 input lines (axons) and 256 outputs (neurons)" (the registered geometry's provenance), so a neuron integrates its own core's 256 axons only, with no inter-core partial sum (coalescing) and no core split across cores that share its inputs (neuron splitting). A deployment that needs either declares it through target_overrides with a note, and its faithfulness names it.

stated.quote: To demonstrate, we built a 5.4 billion transistor chip with 4, 096 neurosynaptic cores interconnected via an intra-chip network that integrates one million programmable spiking neurons and 256 million configurable synapses.
stated.reads: integrates one million programmable spiking neurons

departs.computation: binary synapse times a 9-bit signed integer of its neuron for the type of the axon
departs.location: Supplementary Text S1 'Neurosynaptic Core Operation', PDF p.18, and S8 'Computational Efficiency', PDF p.22
departs.quote: On a core, each axon i is assigned one of four types Gi 2 {0, 1, 2, 3} and each neuron j can individually assign a programmable signed integer SjGi for axon type Gi . Synaptic weight from axon i to neuron j is a product of two terms: wi,j ⇥ SjGi , where wi,j 2 {0, 1}. ... Specifically, a synaptic operation constitutes adding a 9 bit signed integer SjGi to the membrane potential
departs.reads: Synaptic weight from axon i to neuron j is a product of two terms
departs.reason: The toolchain's weight grid is one symmetric signed integer per synapse. A binary synapse scaled by a per-neuron integer chosen by the axon's type is a factored weight law the grid cannot hold, so the registered geometry's 1-bit weights are assumed in its place (scout_chip.md section 5.2).
departs.note: A synapse is a binary connection w_ij in {0, 1} times a 9-bit signed integer S_jG of its axon's type (Supplementary, 'Neurosynaptic core'): the toolchain's weight grid cannot hold the axon-type law; the registered geometry's 1-bit weights are the description's assumption, and the faithfulness names the departure.

unstated.note: A synapse is one binary crossbar point (w_ij in {0, 1}); the source states no count.
The crossbar point is binary (w_ij in {0, 1}), a bit the source does not state as a number; the weight one synapse represents is w_ij times its neuron's 9-bit signed integer for the axon's type.

The source states a leak, not a bias: "the neuron j updates its membrane potential, Vj (t), from its previous value, Vj (t 1), by subtracting its leak" (Table S2 caption). A signed per-neuron leak each time step is a per-neuron constant each cycle, which the description assumes as the on-chip bias.

stated.quote: Table S2: Simplified Neuron Update Equations. TrueNorth’s neuron is an extension of the integrate-and-fire neuron with several operational modes and integrated pseudorandomness
stated.reads: an extension of the integrate-and-fire neuron

unstated.note: A core updates all of its neurons at discrete time steps, and a spike reaches its target axon after a programmed delay of 1 to 15 time steps (Supplementary, 'Neurosynaptic core'): both of the toolchain's LIF variants schedule onto that; the deployment declares one.
The source states no window; the deployment declares it.
The source states no level count; the deployment declares it.

stated.quote: After synaptic events are evaluated, a leak is applied (Lk ), the membrane potential is compared to a threshold (Thr ) and if there is a spike, it is injected into the Router (Spk ) with its predefined route (Fig. S2).
stated.reads: After synaptic events are evaluated, a leak is applied (Lk ), the membrane potential is compared to a threshold

unstated.note: The neuron resets to a programmable value R_j (Table S2), one of several operational modes of the full model (ref. 20): the deployment declares the reset law.

stated.quote: Specifically, a synaptic operation constitutes adding a 9 bit signed integer SjGi to the membrane potential, which is a 20 bit signed integer, when axon Ai (t) = 1 and synaptic connection wi,j = 1.
